explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `fstTarget`, `sndTarget` and `commonTarget` are the library's own opens of Spec of the ring pullback. Each is defined with the library's `kernelComplement`: they are the complements of the zero loci of the kernels of `pullbackSnd`, `pullbackFst` and `toBase` (`toBase` is the composite `f ∘ pullbackFst`). The real content is the library's own lemma `ker_toBase`, which says ker(toBase) = ker(fst) ⊔ ker(snd). The rest of the proof is generic set algebra (`Set.compl_inter`, `Set.inter_comm`) plus the general Mathlib lemma `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_sup`. That lemma is only an ingredient and does not state the theorem. Mathlib has nothing about these library-defined opens or this kernel decomposition. I checked the definitions and the proof's dependencies in the library file.
